precepts.text: The graven images of their gods shall be burned with fire as a cursed and abominable thing.
precepts.point: After the sacrifice he sends in the guard to slay them all, breaks down the images and the house of Baal, and makes it a draught house, so Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

precepts.why:
“The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire.” The silver and gold on them is not to be desired, “for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.” It is not to be brought into the house, “lest thou be a cursed thing like it: but thou shalt utterly detest it, and thou shalt utterly abhor it; for it is a cursed thing.”

That is the law Jehu carried out. He gathered all the worshippers of Baal in subtilty, filled the house of Baal, and after the sacrifice sent in the guard to slay them. Then “they brought forth the images out of the house of Baal, and burned them. And they brake down the image of Baal, and brake down the house of Baal, and made it a draught house unto this day.”

The images were burned with fire and treated as the cursed thing they are. So Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.

precepts.point: Yet Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of the Most High with all his heart, showing that a man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

precepts.why:
“All, except David and Ezekias and Josias, were defective: for they forsook the law of the most High, even the kings of Juda failed.”

Jehu is counted among the defective. He destroyed Baal out of Israel, and the Most High commended him for doing to the house of Ahab all that was in his heart. Yet he departed not from the golden calves in Beth-el and in Dan, and “took no heed to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart.”

Only David, Hezekiah and Josiah stand apart. A man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin.

precepts.text: Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall, for the Most High provides a way to escape temptation.
precepts.point: Yet Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of the Most High with all his heart, showing that a man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

precepts.why:
“Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.” Jehu stood; he executed judgment on the house of Ahab and destroyed Baal, and the Most High promised his children to the fourth generation would sit on the throne. Still he fell, for he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam.

And there was no excuse: “God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” The Most High provides a way to escape. Jehu took no heed.

precepts.text: Not everyone that saith Lord shall enter, but he that doeth the will of the Father, lest the Lord say depart from me.
precepts.point: Yet Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of the Most High with all his heart, showing that a man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

precepts.why:
“Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.” Many will say they prophesied, cast out devils and “done many wonderful works”, and the answer will be, “I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.”

Jehu did wonderful works in the Lord’s name. He destroyed Baal out of Israel. But he did not do the will of the Father with all his heart; he kept the golden calves. Great works do not stand in the place of walking in the law.

precepts.text: The Most High promised Jehu that his children of the fourth generation would sit on Israel's throne, fulfilled in Zachariah.
precepts.point: The end of Zachariah fulfills the word spoken to Jehu, that his sons would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

precepts.why:
The Most High told Jehu, “Because thou hast done well in executing that which is right in mine eyes, and hast done unto the house of Ahab according to all that was in mine heart, thy children of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.”

Zachariah the son of Jeroboam is that fourth generation. He reigned six months, did evil, departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, and Shallum conspired against him and slew him. And Kings says it outright: “This was the word of the Lord which he spake unto Jehu, saying, Thy sons shall sit on the throne of Israel unto the fourth generation. And so it came to pass.”

points: Jehu writes to the rulers of Jezreel who kept Ahab's seventy sons, challenging them to set up a son and fight, but they are exceedingly afraid because two kings could not stand before him.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

points: They submit as his servants, and Jehu's second letter commands them to take the heads of Ahab's seventy sons and bring them to Jezreel by the next day.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

points: The heads are laid in two heaps at the gate, and Jehu slays all that remained of the house of Ahab, his great men, kinsfolk, and priests, until none remained, according to the word spoken by Elijah.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

points: Jehu meets the brethren of Ahaziah going to salute the king's children and has all forty-two of them slain at the pit of the shearing house, guilty by association with the house of Ahab.

points: He takes up Jehonadab the son of Rechab, whose heart is right with his, into the chariot to see his zeal for the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law
